title: Cutting Local Journalists, McClatchy Embraces AI Content
key_facts: McClatchy, which owns about 30 newspapers, made deep layoffs "last month" while saying it remains "deeply committed to local journalism".
The Idaho Statesman cut 10 of 18 reporters and 3 of 4 editors, leaving a staff of nine.
At least 90 unionised journalists and media workers were laid off, before counting editors and the 13 non-union papers.
Earlier this year McClatchy introduced an AI "Content Scaling Agent" that turns staff articles into summaries; unions filed grievances.
McClatchy owner Chatham Asset Management bought it for $312 million in 2020; the company has not cited financial difficulty for the cuts.
Days after the layoffs, an internal email celebrated five new hires for its AI-focused "Content Innovation Lab".
quote_evidence: What makes this particular round of media layoffs unique is what McClatchy is choosing to invest its resources in instead of reporters and editors: artificial intelligence.
“It really feels like McClatchy's strategy is getting out of the journalism business and into the content business,” said Lycklama from the Idaho Statesman.
why_it_matters_hint: Local readers lose reporters, such as city hall coverage, while the owner invests in AI content.
event_date: layoffs announced "last month" (Sept 2026, exact date not stated); article 8 Oct 2026
notes: Opinionated analysis; spokesperson did not respond. Layoff date is not stated, so freshness is NEW (the reporting is new) and the summary says "last month".
